Kidnapped Baby Olothando update

By: Laura Byrne | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We catch up with social worker Portia Marinana, whose heroism has been recognised with a good citizenship award.

Unique Selling Point:
We revisit our inspiring story of two women who solved the mystery of a missing baby and returned her to her devastated mother. Social worker Portia Marinana's dedication to her job has been recognised with the Herald Nelson Mandela University Citizen of the Year Award.

Summary:
Social worker Portia Marinana went above and beyond when she was asked to assist a couple with the registration of their grandchild's birth, and noticed discrepancies on the baby's birth records. She followed her instincts and uncovered a daring kidnapping: the baby had been stolen from her mother on the way home from the hospital. Portia and a colleague were able to track down the baby and return her to her grieving mother. Now, Portia's good work has been recognised.

Script:


VOICEOVER: It was a story of heartbreak, hope… and two unlikely detectives. Last November, baby Olothando was kidnapped from his mother, Noncedo Jali, as she returned home after giving birth at Dora Nginza Hospital in Gqeberha.
UPSOUND: NONCEDO JALI: [CB ARCHIVE] All along I had a feeling that my child was alive somewhere out there.
VOICEOVER: Seven months later, an elderly couple asked social worker Portia Marinana to help them register their grandchild. Portia spotted suspicious discrepancies on the baby’s paperwork.
UPSOUND: PORTIA MARINANA [CB ARCHIVE] The baby's name was tippexed off and was written with a pen... I knew something was wrong.
VOICEOVER: With the help of administration clerk Kaamilah Eagles, Portia identified Noncedo as the baby’s mother… After seven long months, the two were reunited. In September, Portia’s dedication was celebrated, with a Herald NMU Citizen of the Year Award in healthcare.
UPSOUND: PORTIA MARINANA: Social workers will tell you that it's what we do almost on a daily basis. And sometimes at work you can feel very discouraged. So,I still haven't processed it, but it was a great feeling.
VOICEOVER: She has stayed in contact with Noncedo, helping her get a child grant and a new birth certificate.
UPSOUND: PORTIA MARINANA: I wanted to make sure that they have the tools they need to create that bond that was almost lost. They are doing well, exceptionally well. From what I'm observing, he has adjusted very well to his family.
VOICEOVER: The case against alleged kidnapper Amahle Sigam is ongoing.
